item.title: Critical Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator zero day command injection CVE-2026-16812 exploited in the wild
item.description:
A maximum severity operating system command injection vulnerability in a central software defined networking orchestration platform is undergoing active wild exploitation as a zero day. The defect allows remote unauthenticated network adversaries to execute privileged system commands and gain absolute administrative control over host appliances.
Tracked as CVE-2026-16812 with a CVSS score of 10.0, the vulnerability impacts on-premises Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator deployments across versions 5.x, 6.x, and earlier builds. The flaw stems from unsanitized input validation within web administrative interfaces. Threat actors pass malformed network requests to execute shell instructions, export system databases, and harvest device certificates, API tokens, and tenant configurations without requiring user credentials. CISA added the flaw to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog under BOD 26-04, requiring immediate federal mitigation.
Subverting a centralized SD-WAN orchestrator compromises communication channels across the enterprise perimeter. Because orchestrators manage global edge routing profiles, VPN tunnels, and device inventory keys, an administrative takeover allows adversaries to intercept corporate traffic, alter network policies, and execute lateral movement routines targeting connected subnets.
- Upgrade affected VeloCloud Orchestrator instances to patched versions 5.2.3.14, 6.1.3.4, 6.4.2.4, or 7.0.0.1 immediately. - Inspect web access logs for unusual URL path structures or unexpected HTTP requests targeting diagnostic endpoints. - Audit backend system and application logs for unauthorized command execution, database dumps, or key exports. - Restrict network access to management interfaces, gating web console visibility exclusively behind authenticated zero trust reverse proxies.
Network orchestration plane safety relies on rapid patch deployment and strict interface isolation to ensure that centralized control consoles remain completely protected from unauthenticated command injection. #CodeDefence #Arista #VeloCloud #SDWAN #ZeroDay #CommandInjection #CISA #KEV

item.title: Critical OpenWrt DHCPv6 stack overflow vulnerability CVE-2026-53921 allows unauthenticated root code execution
item.description:
A critical stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability residing in a widely deployed open source networking daemon has been resolved, preventing network adjacent threat actors from executing unauthenticated code with root privileges. The flaw permits remote attackers to transmit malformed network packets to overwrite stack memory boundaries.
The security defect, tracked as CVE-2026-53921 with a CVSS score of 9.8, impacts the odhcpd daemon within OpenWrt installations prior to version 24.10.8. The flaw involves an improper bounds check when parsing incoming DHCPv6 REQUEST packets. An attacker on the local network segment or adjacent IPv6 routing path can send tailored packet sequences to trigger a memory write overflow, hijacking daemon execution threads to run arbitrary system binaries as root.
Compromising a core gateway routing service destroys local network isolation boundaries. Because edge routers and access points process all transit traffic, DNS requests, and IP address allocations, a root level takeover allows threat actors to install persistent packet sniffers, redirect network traffic to malicious landing pages, and launch secondary attacks against connected endpoints.
- Update OpenWrt router installations to secure release version 24.10.8 or later immediately to close the buffer overflow path. - Disable unneeded DHCPv6 server components on interfaces exposed to untrusted or public network segments. - Monitor local network telemetry for anomalous high frequency DHCPv6 packet bursts containing non standard option lengths. - Restrict router administration and daemon listening interfaces to trusted internal VLAN boundaries.
Gateway service security depends on strict packet validation within core networking daemons to guarantee that perimeter devices cannot be exploited for unauthenticated remote code execution. #CodeDefence #OpenWrt #DHCPv6 #StackOverflow #RootRCE #NetworkSecurity #AppSec

item.title: CISA adds Fortinet FortiOS SSL VPN patch bypass vulnerability CVE-2025-68686 to KEV catalog
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity regulators have added a critical secure access gateway patch bypass vulnerability to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following active target exploitation in the wild. The flaw enables remote actors to bypass security controls and access sensitive configuration data on perimeter firewalls.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2025-68686, impacts Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN configurations. The issue involves a patch bypass mechanism that allows threat actors to re-exploit legacy vulnerabilities and gain unauthorized access to memory structures. Threat telemetry confirms that adversaries are actively scanning internet-exposed gateways to extract session tokens, cleartext credentials, and system configuration files.
Bypassing perimeter gateway security controls undermines corporate network defenses. Armed with harvested VPN credentials and session tokens, threat actors can bypass single sign-on gates, connect directly to internal subnets, and establish persistent backdoors into corporate cloud and on-premises resources.
- Apply current software maintenance releases and hotfixes published by Fortinet across all FortiOS firewall instances. - Disable SSL-VPN functionality on perimeter appliances if it is not strictly required for business operations. - Inspect VPN authentication logs for anomalous connection sessions originating from unrecognized IP ranges or outdated client tokens. - Enforce mandatory hardware-bound multi-factor authentication across all secure remote access channels.
Perimeter defense resilience requires continuous verification of security patches to ensure that edge access gateways remain fully protected against bypass exploitation techniques. #CodeDefence #Fortinet #FortiOS #SSLVPN #AuthBypass #CISA #KEV #NetworkSecurity
